livespec.repaired_by: bd-ib-4yvurp — version 1 carried a `style`/`column_layout` board with its seven query specifications INLINE under a top-level `queries` array, which the current Create a Board API cannot accept. Version 2 is the same seven chart intents and captions expressed as `type: flexible` query PANELS; the provisioner materializes each `query` below through the Queries API and replaces it with the persisted `query_id` plus the `query_annotation_id` that carries the caption.
livespec.purpose: Show the post-hoc Red share and its supporting TDD signals, grouped by repository and by adapter, over the terminal dispatcher.calibration span.
livespec.idempotence_key: name — the provisioner GETs /1/boards, matches on this exact name, and PUTs the existing board rather than creating a second one.
livespec.panel_identity_key: query_panel.caption — a Query cannot be listed, fetched or updated through the API, so the only observable record of which persisted query a panel holds is the QUERY ANNOTATION that names it. The provisioner uses the caption as the annotation `name`, matches an existing annotation on it, and stores a fingerprint of the query specification in the annotation `description`; an unchanged fingerprint reuses the persisted query, a changed one persists a new query and re-points the SAME annotation at it. That is what keeps a re-apply from accumulating a second set of panels.
livespec.dataset_is_not_a_panel_field: Each panel's dataset comes from the Queries API URL the specification is POSTed to (/1/queries/<dataset>), not from a field inside the panel: `query_panel.dataset` is read-only on the board resource, so sending it is rejected.
livespec.layout: A deterministic, reviewable 12-column layout committed as explicit coordinates with layout_generation=manual: the two share panels sit side by side on the top row, then the gap-median heatmap beside the order-guard refusals, then cycles-against-assertions beside the suite-green panel, and the classification-coverage panel spans the full width at the bottom because an unknown count is read as a whole-population figure.
livespec.every_share_query_excludes_unknown: A dispatch whose Red count was never observed is classified 'unknown' and is FILTERED OUT of every share query. Counting it would let a dropped signal read as a healthy run, which is the one failure mode this board exists to catch.
livespec.suite_green_is_broader_than_no_red_produ: Do NOT read tdd.suite_green_count as 'product code landed without a Red'. red_green_replay reaches its TDD-Suite-Green-* leg from TWO branches: product impl .py staged with no open Red (a refactor or behaviour-preserving chore), AND a PASSING TEST-ONLY change under a non-feat/fix subject, which touches no product .py at all. Measured on this slice's own commit series 2026-10-02 — 8 commits, 6 Red, 6 Green, suite_green_count 2, both of them test-and-docs commits with no product impl — which falsified the plan research's framing of leg 5 as 'product code with no Red at all'. The count is a useful signal paired with the gap median and the first-write flag; it is not a verdict on its own.
livespec.live_validation_owed: The query shapes below have not been accepted by the live Honeycomb API from the build sandbox; plan child bd-ib-i56nut owns the live leg and records the created board id plus a query result containing the new calibration fields.

payload.name: livespec factory test-first order (TDD calibration)
payload.description: Post-hoc Red share and supporting TDD order signals per terminal dispatch, by repository and adapter. A dispatch is post-hoc when its first product write happened outside an open Red, or when its median Red-to-Green gap is under the configured threshold — the stash-and-unstash shape the red_green_replay commit hook structurally cannot see. Source semantics for every tdd.* field are in _dispatcher_tdd_signals; the motivating fleet-wide measurement is in plan/factory-test-first-enforcement/research/opening-research-2026-09-30.md.

query_panel.caption: Post-hoc Red share by repository (1.0 = every classified dispatch was post-hoc)
Post-hoc Red share by implement adapter
Red-to-Green gap median per dispatch — the load-bearing signal (seconds)
Order-guard refusals per dispatch, by repository and adapter
Cycles against assertions — one Red per acceptance assertion is the target
Suite-green commits (admitted by the full suite, not by a failing test) among dispatches whose first write preceded a Red
Classification coverage — how many dispatches are unclassifiable (a telemetry gap, not a clean run)
